title: TRIAD declared deletion roots
description: The one configuration file that declares every folder a host's code may delete (R-CLEANUP). The declaration adds to the ownership proof and never replaces it; deletion code refuses a target outside a declared root. A missing or invalid file deletes nothing: the deletion command refuses (host fault) and automatic prunes skip with a one-line note; a host ships a default file (owner, D-DELETION-BY-CODE-20261004).

role.description: The name an AI may choose; unique within the file.

root.description: The one folder under which this role's deletions happen; it covers its whole subtree and is never a glob: repository-relative (resolved against the git top-level of the working directory), or beginning with $TMPDIR, ~ or $HOST_DIR (the directory that holds the host's own deletion command).

proof.description: The ownership proof R-CLEANUP already requires, never a name shape: a marker file the host writes, an allocation record, membership in a packet the host owns, or a git-registered worktree inside the declared root. A marker is a regular file of that name directly in the folder to delete; alloc-record and inside-owned-packet are proved only inside the host's own sweep, so the deletion command refuses them.

min_age_s.description: The host's age floor for this role, in seconds, for sweeps and general deletion requests. R-CLEANUP's explicit named-round close and already-started deletion resumption are not held back by the sweep floor; their other checks remain required.
